Every other board takes the rule's default max(2, ceil(5 % of its connections)), with `connections` the router's `board_statistics.connections.maximum_count` from the arm's result manifest (gate_totals.rs `default_band`), the larger of the two arms as the gate takes it: a count of the board as loaded, not of a route. The pair does not move it, and neither do the engine changes since K15.37's run (K15.40, K15.41, K15.42, K15.44, K15.45: routes, the fill model, the floors and the cleanup, not the count of connections as loaded): K15.37's records (target/orchestrator/k1537/out/records.json) give maximum_count 852 (pcu) and 331 (canary-pwr) in both arms of each, and the orchestrator's check on combined main ebde9a2 (target/orchestrator/k1543pre/runs, release) gives the same: 852 in both pcu arms and 331 in both canary-pwr arms. helper.what: K15.14's helper, unchanged (the same sha256 as K15.14's `helper`): `prepare` (the boards, from `boards`), `run` (the registration's `commands`, verbatim) and `collect` (records.json for the gate and table.md, from the arms each row's `commands` lists and the registered `metrics`); nothing in it names K15.14's flag or arms. `collect` also computes K15.13's pour-guard count, which is not a registered metric here and so is not recorded; table.md's 'pours guarded' column is 0 in every arm and is not read

grader.what: the measuring instruments registered at ebde9a2: the grader's files (the metric definitions and the oracle) and the plugin files that make the arms' flags. The test pins the three tools/kicad-oracle files, the script and the helper; amendment 1 re-reads all of them at K15_43_COMMIT, and a different hash there is named with the commit that changed it. A later change to a pinned file goes in `amendments` and updates the pin in the same change

grading: per row, pcb-off then pcb-on; pcb-on with SHARE_GRADE_WITH its pcb-off arm, so a session byte-identical to the baseline's copies its grade (summary grade_shared_with). Under the board's own rules (rules = project: the row's .kicad_pro and .kicad_dru, hashed in rules_files), the same oracle, metrics and manufacturing types as K13.6, K14.6 and K15.14. kicad-cli only while `pgrep -x kicad-cli` shows none, one job at a time, no other heavy run at the same time; the grader is the one in `grader` (K15.44's below_minimum against the minimum KiCad's DRC checks)
limits: K15.37's: every router call (the load check and the route) under ulimit -v 8000000 (ROUTE_MEMORY_KB) and timeout -k 10 300 (ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S); every route with `--max-passes 2 --timeout 240` after the plugin's flags. A call that hits ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S or is killed by a signal (exit status 124 or above) is aborted = 1 and not graded. A route the router's own --timeout stopped (result manifest final_state TIMED_OUT) depends on the machine's speed, so its row is not judged (validity (b)). The pair costs route time, less than in K15.37 after K15.41. Seen with the pair (K15.41's runs, target/orchestrator/k1541/runs/, on K15.37's snapshot, load 2.5-4): complex_hierarchy 3.7 s (K15.37 44.3 s), interf_u 10.7 s (20.5 s), pcu 187.4 s (189.6 s), canary-pwr 97.2 s (153.2 s), pcie 49.7 s COMPLETED (K15.37 timed out at 280.2 s), kit-dev-coldfire 192.3 s COMPLETED (timed out at 245.7 s); the same binary without the pair took 25.0 s (pcie) and 118.8 s (kit-dev), so the pair still costs 2.0 x and 1.6 x there. Rows near the deadline: pcu with the pair took 187-213 s (K15.41 204.0 s at load 3.9-4.9, K15.42 192.8-212.8 s, K15.45's pcb-off 180.3 s), against 240 s; pocketsdr-v3-0 timed out in both arms of K15.30 and K15.37 and may again. If pcu or canary-pwr is TIMED_OUT in either arm the measurement is 'not measured' (must_judge); run the registered run with no other load on the machine. The registered handling of a slower row is validity (b) plus guard (4), not a longer deadline. Estimated time: 34 calls. K15.37's run took 45 min for its 34 calls (09:42:31 to 10:27:32), with 2 x 240 s on pocketsdr-v3-0, 245.7 s and 280.2 s on the two rows that timed out only with the pair, and 465.7 s (pcb-off) and 797.2 s (pcb-on) of routing over the 14 judged rows. Now the two rows no longer time out (about -230 s and -100 s of routing for them), complex_hierarchy and canary-pwr route faster, and moteus's island repair adds about 10-15 s; the plugin's snapshot, import and the kicad-cli grading of every pcb-on session that differs from pcb-off's are as before. Expected: about 35-50 min; the bound if every call hit ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S is 34 x about 330 s = 3.1 h

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: summary via_in_pad: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py's vias_in_pads on the routed board minus the input board's, floored at 0 (D8)
metric_definitions.below_minimum: summary below_minimum: routed tracks and vias (whose nanometre copper key the input board does not have) under the minimum track width, via diameter or via drill that KiCad's DRC checks (`oracle_lib.effective_minimums`, K15.44): Board Setup's value, replaced by the last unconditional .kicad_dru rule (no condition, no layer clause, not `severity ignore`) with a `min` for `track_width`, `via_diameter` or `hole_size`; summed. The summary also records board_minimums_mm, board_minimums_from and board_setup_minimums_mm
metric_definitions.manufacturing_breaches: summary manufacturing_breaches: the routing-caused KiCad DRC items (Q22.2's copper basis) of the types clearance, hole_clearance, hole_to_hole, copper_edge_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, solder_mask_bridge, shorting_items, summed
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: the signal: summary unconnected, kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the routed board after --refill-zones
metric_definitions.zone_zone_unconnected: secondary: the routed board's unconnected items (routed/drc.json, or the shared grade's) whose items are all zones: a pour split into islands that KiCad cannot join (K15.13's count)
metric_definitions.zone_zone_zones: the distinct (net, layer) zones those items name
metric_definitions.router_incomplete: the router's own incomplete connections at the end: the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.incomplete_count (work/<name>.result.json)
metric_definitions.kicad_less_router: secondary: kicad_unconnected - router_incomplete, how far KiCad's count is above the router's (K15.25 on pcu-76163c7: 36 off and 35 on; on canary-pwr-95882f00: 13 and 12)
metric_definitions.drc_real: guard (2): the sum of summary routing_caused_by_type (the grader's drc_real), every type
metric_definitions.route_seconds: guard (4): summary route_s, the routing call's wall-clock seconds
metric_definitions.connections: the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.maximum_count: the board's connections as the router loaded it, the default noise band's base
metric_definitions.input_unconnected: summary input_unconnected: kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the stripped input board

validity: checked before keep_rule, per row: (a) both settings reached the router: each pcb-on arm's result manifest (OUT/<row>/pcb-on/work/<stem>.result.json) has settings_snapshot.pour_fill_target true and settings_snapshot.pour_fill_contacts true, and no pcb-off arm's has either true (unset, so absent); a row whose pcb-on session is byte-identical to pcb-off's (summary grade_shared_with set) is judged as it is (the settings changed no route there) and named; (b) the row is judged when both its arms have aborted 0, graded true and final_state COMPLETED; a row COMPLETED in pcb-off and TIMED_OUT in pcb-on (the pair needs more than the registered 240 s router deadline) is left out by (b) like any other, its pcb-on result depending on the machine's speed, but it is named with both route times and guard (4) counts it; (c) amendment 1 is written before the first arm and `cargo test -p freerouting-dev --test prereg_k15_43` passes in TREE. A row that fails (a) or (b), or whose board is missing, is left out of the judgement and reported by name with its reason; the keep rule, guards (2) and (3) and the set noise are then over the judged rows only (guard (4) as it says). The measurement is 'not measured' (decision_table) only when fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows are judged, pcu-76163c7 or canary-pwr-95882f00 is not judged (must_judge), or (c) fails
guards: (1) in every arm that runs and is graded, judged row or not: manufacturing_breaches = 0, below_minimum = 0 and via_in_pad = 0, absolutely (decided 2026-10-20: routing never breaks the board's manufacturing rules; routing-quality.md, order of importance items 1 and 2); the gate's HARD lines of the verdict pair and the reported pair, and summary.json for the rows left out. (2) routing-caused DRC not up: the sum of drc_real over the judged rows in pcb-on is at most pcb-off's. (3) no row worse than its own noise band (K15.14's guard, decided 2026-10-21): on every judged row, pcb-on's kicad_unconnected is at most pcb-off's + the row's band, the totals rule's per-row band (canary-pwr-95882f00 10, every other row max(2, ceil(5 % of its connections)), noise_why). (4) route time: the sum of route_seconds in pcb-on over the judged rows and over every row COMPLETED in pcb-off and TIMED_OUT in pcb-on (validity (b); its pcb-on value is the deadline, about 240.1 s, a lower bound of its time) is at most 1.25 x the sum of pcb-off's over the same rows
keep_rule: kept when validity holds (at least 3 distinct rows judged, pcu-76163c7 and canary-pwr-95882f00 among them, (c)), guard (1) holds, the signal improves (S: the sum of pcb-on's kicad_unconnected over the judged rows is lower than pcb-off's by more than the set noise sqrt(sum of the bands squared), noise_why; strictly more, as the gate computes it) and guards (2), (3) and (4) hold
keep_rule_by_hand: from OUT/records.json and OUT/table.md (`python3 -I TREE/tools/bench/k15_all_pours.py collect TREE/docs/roadmap/prereg/K15.43.json OUT`) and the gate (TREE's freerouting-dev, the commands of heavy_run's last step, with --prereg ROOT's docs/roadmap/prereg/K15.43.json as amended): `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json --write-baseline`, then `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json --all-pairs`, each with `--left-out ROW=REASON` for every row validity (b) leaves out (K15.21). The verdict pair's 'totals verdict' line is S, with the set noise it prints; its HARD lines and the reported pair's are guard (1); guards (2)-(4) are summed by hand from records.json (guard (4) with the rows validity (b) names); validity (a) from the result manifests and (b) from table.md's state column. The reverse pair is there for its HARD lines only; its totals verdict is the verdict pair's mirror and is not read

decision_table.not measured: fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows judged, pcu-76163c7 or canary-pwr-95882f00 not judged, or validity (c) fails (a row left out by validity (a) or (b) does not by itself make the measurement 'not measured': it is reported by name and the other rows are judged): K15.43 stays [~] naming the rows and reasons; nothing changes in the product; the rows are run again only after the cause is fixed (a longer timeout_s or a fix), under an amendment naming it, with nothing else changed
decision_table.breach: the measurement is not 'not measured' and guard (1) fails in any graded arm (of a judged row or not): K15.43 stays [~] naming the arm, row and items; the breach is fixed in an item of its own (a pcb-on breach that pcb-off lacks is a defect of the pair; one in pcb-off is a defect of today's default), then the registered run repeats at the fixed commit under an amendment; until then `router.pour_fill_contacts` and `router.pour_fill_target` stay opt-in, unset in both profiles. For a pcb-on breach that pcb-off lacks the plugin does not offer `router.pour_fill_contacts` until the fix (K15.37's option: the options.py field and its to_args line, the Advanced tab's checkbox, its plugin tests and the plugin handover's row are removed; K15.30's `pour_fill_target` option, measured alone, stays); a breach in pcb-off leaves both options as they are (decided 2026-10-20: fix gains, don't remove them; never ship below-minimum copper)
decision_table.not kept, guard: none of the above, S holds and any of guards (2), (3), (4) fails over the judged rows: both settings stay opt-in, unset in both profiles, and the plugin keeps both options (`pour_fill_target` K15.30's and `pour_fill_contacts` K15.37's: the options.py fields, the Advanced tab's checkboxes, plugin tests), off in both profiles; the checkbox tooltip of `pour_fill_contacts` and the handover's row are updated with this measurement's totals and the two owner boards' numbers without private board names (K15.37's tooltip carries K15.37's); DIVERGENCES' `pour_fill_contacts` and `pour_fill_target` entries (board model) and the 'Not in `enhanced`' docs of board/pour_contacts.rs and autoroute/pour_target.rs get the numbers; K15.43's note names the failing guard and its rows, and a follow-up item may fix the cost and measure again under a new registration (fix gains, don't remove them)
decision_table.not kept, no gain: neither of the above, and S fails over the judged rows: both settings stay opt-in, unset in both profiles, and the plugin keeps both options (`pour_fill_target` K15.30's and `pour_fill_contacts` K15.37's: the options.py fields, the Advanced tab's checkboxes, plugin tests), off in both profiles; the checkbox tooltip of `pour_fill_contacts` and the handover's row are updated with this measurement's totals and the two owner boards' numbers without private board names (K15.37's tooltip carries K15.37's); DIVERGENCES' `pour_fill_contacts` and `pour_fill_target` entries (board model) and the 'Not in `enhanced`' docs of board/pour_contacts.rs and autoroute/pour_target.rs get the numbers; K15.43's note records the table
decision_table.kept: none of the above: validity, guard (1), S and guards (2), (3), (4) all hold over the judged rows: `router.pour_fill_contacts` and `router.pour_fill_target` both join the ENHANCED table (crates/freerouting/src/settings/profile.rs) as true, in one change (they are measured as a pair; contacts alone is worse than unset on pcu, K15.31); tests/settings_defaults.rs pins enhanced's true for both and legacy's unset; DIVERGENCES' 'Profile `enhanced`' section gets a line per setting with this measurement's totals, and its board-model entries and the 'Not in `enhanced`' docs of autoroute/pour_target.rs and board/pour_contacts.rs say they are enhanced's; `legacy` unchanged: `PARITY_SET=tools/bench/sets/connection-parity.txt tools/parity-check.sh --no-probes` 7 of 7 exact. K15.30's and K15.37's plugin options are removed, because with the profile carrying the settings the fields would add flags that are already set and could not switch them off (a user who wants Java's rules picks profile legacy): the RouteOptions fields `pour_fill_target` and `pour_fill_contacts` in kicad-plugin/freerouting_rs/options.py with their `to_args` lines, `to_dict`, `from_dict` and `from_form` branches and the options table in its docstring, the two checkboxes of the Advanced tab's Flow group (plugin.py / the dialog), their plugin tests (test_options.py, test_route_dialog.py, test_snapshot.py's every-K09-option check) and the plugin handover's rows (docs/development/kicad-plugin.md). A saved options file with a `pour_fill_target` or `pour_fill_contacts` key is read with the key ignored (`RouteOptions.from_dict` reads only the keys it knows; schema 6 stays, and a test pins that a file with the old keys loads without error and adds no pour flag), so a board that had one on routes with the profile's settings, which are on, and a board that had it off now has it on as well; `to_dict` no longer writes the keys. The plugin passes nothing for either setting (the profile carries them)
decision_table.order: the rows are tried in the order not measured, breach, not kept no gain, not kept guard, kept; the first whose condition holds decides, so every outcome maps to exactly one row

report: per row and arm: kicad_unconnected (input_unconnected), zone_zone_unconnected and zone_zone_zones, router_incomplete and kicad_less_router, manufacturing_breaches, below_minimum, via_in_pad, routing_caused_by_type and drc_real, route_seconds, final_state, settings_snapshot.pour_fill_target and settings_snapshot.pour_fill_contacts, board_statistics.connections.maximum_count, aborted, session_sha256 and whether the grade is shared; the rows left out of the judgement and why (a row COMPLETED in pcb-off and TIMED_OUT in pcb-on with both route times); the totals over the judged rows, the set noise and every band; for pcu-76163c7 and canary-pwr-95882f00 the comparison with the numbers in seen_before_registration; for moteus-moteus-c1 the comparison with K15.42's and K15.45's sessions (`pcb-off` 9f998f1d, `pcb-on` f286d7f6); for pcie-active-backplane and kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 both arms' final_state and route_seconds; the below_minimum figures by kind (summary below_minimum_by_kind) and board_minimums_from for the rows with a .kicad_dru; which rows each guard failed on
known_effects: K15.37's run (engine 40c9f7f) kept S (338 -> 272 over 14 judged rows, noise 59.34) and failed guard (2) (drc_real 12 -> 27: interf_u +6, moteus +9, openmuscle +1, nudac -1) and guard (4) (1.95 x). Since then: K15.41 made the pair's route time on the slow rows far lower (complex_hierarchy 44.3 s -> 3.7 s, pcie and kit-dev-coldfire complete); K15.42 took interf_u's and openmuscle's added violations to 0 and moteus's from 13 to 6 (`isolated_copper` 5, `track_dangling` 1, against `pcb-off`'s 4); K15.45 left moteus as K15.42 did. Estimates from the seen runs, which this run tests and does not assume: guard (2) is likely to fail on moteus (6 against 4, +2) unless the other judged rows come down by 2 in total (nudac was -1, the others 0 in K15.37); guard (4) is likely to still fail, about 1.3-1.6 x: K15.37's pcb-off sum over the same 16 rows was 679.9 s, and the seen pcb-on times are lower than K15.37's by about 230 s on pcie and kit-dev, 40 s on complex_hierarchy and 10-50 s on canary-pwr and moteus, but pcie and kit-dev-coldfire still cost 2.0 x and 1.6 x their same-machine pcb-off times and K15.37's pcb-off times (40.9 s, 173.3 s) were taken on a busier machine than K15.41's (25.0 s, 118.8 s). The registered table is the repository's keep rule (routing-quality.md), with the thresholds unchanged (decided 2026-10-22), so 'not kept, guard' is the likely outcome on guard (4) again; the numbers then go into the plugin options' tooltips. The signal is closer than in K15.37: the orchestrator's check on ebde9a2 gives pcu 47 -> 26 (K15.37 47 -> 20) and canary-pwr 40 -> 26, -35 together against -41 in K15.37, and K15.37's other 12 judged rows gained 25 in all, so on the same 14 rows S would be about -60 against a noise of 59.34, and if pcie-active-backplane and kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 are now judged too (noise about 67.09 with pocketsdr-v3-0 out) S fails unless they gain too (K15.41: pcie 5 -> 4, kit-dev 25 -> 22 against K15.37's pcb-off); 'not kept, no gain' is possible as well. With both settings the router's incomplete count is within 1 of KiCad's unconnected on pcu and canary-pwr in K15.37's run (pcu 20 unconnected against 21 incomplete, canary-pwr 26 against 27): the router counts a pad the fill does not reach as open and, with the target, routes the islands together (K15.31). Alone, `pour_fill_contacts` counts the open islands but does not route them (pcu 48, canary-pwr 38 at K15.31), which is why only the pair is measured. Both arms import the session whole, as the plugin does (fix_existing off), on stripped boards with no input copper
stop_rule: one registered run per row and arm; no reruns with other settings; an aborted arm is recorded and not rerun. A rerun after a validity or guard (1) failure is an amendment naming the fix (decision_table). Any change after the first number goes in `amendments` with its reason
